claim: The authors became optimistic that a whole adult mammal or bird brain could be reconstructed within the next decade
quote: reconstructing the nervous system of an entire adult mammal (or bird) brain can be achieved in the next decade

claim: Hot-knife partitioning combined with ion milling stands out as the conceptual advance in acquisition
quote: the combination of hot-knife sample partitioning and ion milling stands out as a conceptual advance

claim: The best AI tracing algorithms make errors at about the rate of a moderately motivated human
quote: makes errors at about the rate of a moderately motivated human

claim: Human tracing errors are uncorrelated (inattention) and fixable by redundancy, whereas different algorithms fail at the same places
quote: Different computer algorithms, on the other hand, tend to fail at the same places in the data set

claim: On VEM data of sufficient quality, expert humans consistently correct almost all algorithm errors, so the data hold the full circuit information
quote: can consistently (across experts) correct almost all of those errors

claim: The hybrid approach creates an over-segmentation: few merges, each neurite split into many supervoxels for humans to join
quote: This situation is called an over segmentation and human proofreading can be performed by simply inspecting each segment

claim: Supervoxel agglomeration and skeleton tracing both cost at least about 0.5 h of human time per mm of neurite
quote: at least about 0.5 h per mm of neurite

claim: The two proofreading approaches cost the same because both require every location to be viewed by a human
quote: both approaches require that all locations in the VEM data set are viewed by one or more humans

claim: Confidence-steered targeted proofreading cut the effort for a given reliability by orders of magnitude in some cases
quote: reduced the total proofreading effort needed to reach a given reconstruction reliability by orders of magnitude

claim: The surge in machine segmentation is likely due to renewed focus on cell-boundary detection
quote: renewed focus on the key step in segmentation: the detection of cell boundaries

claim: Flood-filling networks feed the previous iteration's in-probability back as input, building implicit shape priors into voxel classification
quote: A feedback path makes the previous iteration’s ‘in’-probability part of the classifier input, automatically incorporating implicit shape priors

claim: FIB-SBEM reaches block-face increments as low as 2 nm, against about 20 nm for diamond-knife SBEM
quote: Block-face increments as low as 2 nm have been demonstrated

claim: FIB-SBEM's lateral resolution nears TEM because ion milling tolerates much larger electron exposure than diamond-knife SBEM
quote: because FIB-based material removal tolerates a much larger electron exposure than DiK-SBEM

claim: FIB-SBEM's one big drawback is a field of view limited to a few tens of microns along the ion-beam axis
quote: is limited to a few tens of microns along the axis of the ion beam

claim: Embedded stained brain can be cut with a heated, lubricated diamond knife into thick slabs with minimal loss at the interface
quote: slabs between 10 and 30 mm thick using a lubricated and heated diamond knife

claim: Hot-knife slabs combined with FIB-SBEM should have no sample-size limit while giving data good enough for near error-free automatic extraction
quote: should have no limit on sample size

claim: A single single-beam FIB-SBEM would take thousands of years for a whole mouse brain; parallel slabs on many machines cut wall-clock time
quote: It would take thousands of years to acquire FIB-SBEM data for a whole mouse (bird) brain

claim: Serial-section TEM was used for every whole-brain data set then available
quote: SSTEM was used for all currently available whole-brain datasets

claim: SSTEM data are harder to analyse automatically, likely from anisotropic resolution and slice-to-slice jitter
quote: likely due to the highly anisotropic resolution and to slice-to-slice jitter

claim: TEM fields of view are bounded by the 3 mm grid, too small for bird-brain slices up to 13 x 10 mm
quote: which cannot exceed the standard TEM grid’s 3 mm outer diameter

claim: Wide-field TEM read by a camera array reaches net imaging rates of about 50 MHz
quote: net imaging rates of about 50 MHz using a TEM that is read out with a camera array

claim: ATUM's z-resolution could be improved by imaging at multiple tilt angles or landing energies
quote: could be improved by the acquisition of multiple images at different tilt angles or different landing energies

claim: A multi-beam SEM with up to 91 beams has been designed and is sold by Carl Zeiss Microscopy
quote: with up to 91 beams has been designed and is being sold by Carl Zeiss Microscopy

claim: MSEM has worked on ATUM sections on Kapton tape, but an attempt to combine it with diamond-knife SBEM hit unexpected difficulties
quote: to combine MSEM and DiK-SBEM has run into unexpected difficulties

claim: Combining MSEM with FIB milling is hampered by slow material removal and MSEM's need for a planar surface beyond the imaged area
quote: known difficulties being the slow speed of material removal and the need of the MSEM for a planar sample surface

claim: Gas cluster ion beam milling, knife-less with a large FOV and smooth surface, may be a way out
quote: The emergence of a mode of knife-less material removal that has a large FOV and leaves a smooth sample surface

claim: Imaged-neuron counts double about every 3.6 years, slower than the two-year Moore's-law doubling
quote: estimate the doubling time for the number of imaged neurons arriving at a value of 3.6 years

claim: The extrapolation predicts mouse/bird whole-brain data sets in 2049 and human in 2084, perhaps too pessimistically
quote: predicts’ such data sets for mouse (bird) and human for the years 2049 and 2084

claim: The authors invoke Amara's law: new technologies' impact is overestimated short-term and underestimated long-term
quote: the impact of novel technologies is almost always overestimated in the short term but underestimated in the long term

claim: A 2019 corrigendum corrected the adult fruit fly brain count to about 100,000 neurons; 250,000 is the whole nervous system
quote: is according to [2] about 100 000 and not 250 000

claim: The FFN-beats-U-Net comparison on FIB-25 may have favoured FFNs because the U-Net test was months older
quote: because the U-Net test was, while being the latest one available, several months older
